result.title: SEOYUN: Refusal-Inducing Exam Documents for AI-Glasses Pipelines
result.comment: 10 pages; research framework and analytical limits; no empirical efficacy results. Includes an author reflection in Korean in Appendix C
result.summary: Camera-equipped glasses can convert an examination page into a query to a vision-language model (VLM). Device detection addresses possession; a complementary question is whether an examination document can reduce the usefulness of an unauthorized capture. We present SEOYUN, an application-specific framework for refusal-inducing exam documents, with optical and encoder-level interventions as extensions. We use reverse jailbreaking to describe the direction of the objective: inducing abstention rather than bypassing refusal. Refusal induction and defensive visual prompt injection already have precedents; our contribution is a threat model, analytical limits, and an evaluation protocol for examination use. We distinguish refusal from correct-answer leakage, show why removing an added dummy option is not itself a reduction in the original answer space, and derive a sampling comparison under explicitly stated camera assumptions. The protocol separates digital, simulated, and physical inputs and requires held-out evaluation after subject-specific selection. A local CSAT candidate corpus and rendering harness have been prepared, but this version reports no model-performance measurements, physical validation, or human-subject results. Accordingly, SEOYUN is a research framework, not a validated defense or a basis for allegations against individuals.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SEOYUN 框架，探讨能否通过设计「诱导拒答」的考试文档，降低 AI 眼镜拍摄后 VLM 作答的可用性，给出威胁模型、分析性界限，以及区分数字、模拟与物理输入的评测协议，本版本尚未报告任何模型效果测量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 encoder 级视觉干预与「拒答不等于答案泄漏减少」的论证，可能可供核查 VLM 输出是否真依赖视觉 latent 内容及如何做因果性评测；但仅有框架、无实证，联系尚属推测。
